in.name: Orcish Bowmasters
in.why: Goldfish -0.025, second-worst and outside the noise floor; its payoff is MILLING, and the self-mill package log 003 floated was never built, so it converts a death into nothing this deck uses. Orcish Bowmasters is a BRACKET-4 Game Changer the old bracket-3 ceiling forbade (the candidate scan dropped it with six others): two mana, flash, one damage on entry and on every extra card an opponent draws, then an Army that grows with it — a body, a clock and a tax on the three draw engines this pod runs. Predicted: noncombat damage up, kills_by_ability up. Game Changers 3 -> 4, which bracket 4 does not cap.

in.name: Bastion of Remembrance
in.why: Cordial puts its counters on creatures dying in the same wipe (prescription cut #1, +0.009 inside the noise floor). Bastion was PROVEN in drain-v1: 19 casts, 117 triggers — a death drain on an ENCHANTMENT, so an opponent's wipe pays instead of costing, which is the failure log 006 records. Cast late (72 castable turns): that is the `permanent-cast-priority` class and there is NO hint for it in Forge (AICastPreference is don't-cast only), so it is read as a floor. Cites strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance.

in.name: Indulging Patrician
in.why: Legion's Landing is a 1/1 lifelink token and a flip land (-0.005). Indulging Patrician is three mana, flying, lifelink, and drains EACH OPPONENT 3 at your end step whenever you gained 3 that turn — with Conqueror back, every point an opponent loses gains you that much, so the Patrician converts the gain half into drain without being a loop. It is the gain-to-drain the branch lost when Conqueror left (life gained -14.5). Predicted: drain up, life gained up, evasive share up. Cites strategy:life-as-resource.lifegain-engine.

in.name: Shared Animosity
in.why: THE PILOT'S OWN RULE, 2026-10-01: 'lords and anthems that just add +1/+1 counter are weak... there's one I cut I should add back that gives each creature +1/+1 for each attacking creature of the same kind, and that's the only lord/anthem I want to see.' Shared Animosity is that card and git shows it was in this list twice before. It is +1/+0 per OTHER attacking Vampire, so it scales with the width eminence creates instead of adding a flat point, and as an ENCHANTMENT a creature wipe does not take it. Patchwork Banner is the flat version it outclasses (-0.006). This is the staged answer to 'close by T6' and to the combat-damage row drain-v1 lost. Cites strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density.lord-exposure.

in.name: Mirkwood Bats
in.why: THE WORST CARD IN THE DECK BY BOTH INSTRUMENTS. Goldfish card-value -0.035, the only card outside the 0.015 noise floor on the negative side; Forge, 200 games at the pinned harness: cast 17, 61 turns on the battlefield, ZERO activations — and docs/gotchas-bench.md already records 0 for 59 castings under both AI profiles. An outlet the AI cannot use is not an outlet. Mirkwood Bats drains EACH OPPONENT 1 whenever you CREATE OR SACRIFICE A TOKEN: eminence mints a token on every other Vampire cast and the remaining four outlets eat them, so it is paid by the engine the deck already runs rather than by a new one. EDHREC rank 228, the best-ranked drain card on the pilot's own candidate list. Predicted: drain_dealt up. Cites strategy:aristocrats.

in.name: Smothering Tithe

in.name: Malakir Bloodwitch

changes.why: v1.2.0 at BRACKET 4 — the pilot's call, 2026-10-01, after drain-v1's 200-game arm read as an overall downgrade: 'bring back bloodthirsty conqueror... let's go full on Tier 4... I want something that can close or win by T6'. READING B IS REVERSED: Conqueror stays, so Conqueror+Vito and Conqueror+Sanguine Bond are two-card infinites the deck carries by construction and that is accepted. THE LOOP IS NOT THE PLAN: nothing tutors for it, Exquisite Blood stays out. The clock target is stated honestly as T7-T8 — a T6 POD kill needs ~120 life across three opponents and Sanctum Seeker with six attackers doubled by Bloodletter is ~12 to each a combat. WHAT drain-v1 TAUGHT (same harness, 200 games each arm): drain 6.59 -> 10.66, +4.07 [0.45, 7.69] EXCLUDES ZERO, so the five adds that played do raise drain; but life_gained -14.5, biggest_hit -1.95 and combat damage -16.6 mean (median -3.0, tail-driven) all excluded zero, and essentially all of that was Conqueror's departure — he was the gain engine and the deck's biggest body. So: Conqueror in, the five proven adds in, the lords NOT cut as deeply (7 -> 5 plus Shared Animosity, where drain-v1 went 7 -> 4), and bracket-4 mana. THE OBJECTIVE IS DELIBERATELY THE SAME LINE drain-v1 MISSED (10.66 against >= 12), so the two branches are directly comparable and the question is exactly 'does Conqueror's return plus Mirkwood Bats and Indulging Patrician clear it'. Combat damage, biggest hit, life gained and win rate are read as exploratory with their intervals, and the branch is NOT proposable if combat damage or biggest hit falls with an interval excluding zero. Harness PINNED as before: standard-v3 / overrides 8c347642 / mm-edgar-vampires (aif7c3b6a8) / patches c22ecaf3. No pay-X sweeper is staged, so the PumpAllAi patch is deliberately NOT made yet and the champion's 200 games stay the comparison. EVERY ADD IS CAST-CHECKED BEFORE THE ARM (the 2026-10-01 gate).

derived.name: THE OBJECTIVE
derived.what: One falsifiable threshold, written when the branch was OPENED and before anything was measured.
derived.why: It is the only thing here that can fail. Everything else is a description of what changed; this is the claim the branch made about itself, graded against its own minimum detectable difference.

derived.name: THE MANA
derived.what: Karsten's hypergeometric source targets against the pip distribution each list actually has, and the on-curve probability the base achieves.
derived.why: Deterministic, and the nine sampled rows cannot see it. A branch that changes its spells changes its pip distribution, so the target moves underneath the base — which is why the GAP is the figure and not the source count.

derived.name: PRIMARY AND EXPLORATORY
derived.what: The objective is the one pre-registered test. The twelve rows are a family of looks, each with an interval on its difference, and a row's verdict is Holm-corrected across the family.
derived.why: Twelve rows at alpha 0.05 with no correction is one false 'better' in every other report. `experiment.py` pre-registers `win_rate` for the same reason. Measured over 42 tracked reports before shipping: Holm flips no verdict — the MDE rule was already near Bonferroni at the top rank — so this is what a verdict means, not which rows carry one.

derived.name: MDE
derived.what: The minimum detectable difference: the smallest gap this many games could resolve at 95% confidence.
derived.why: A row marked `noise` is NOT a row where nothing happened. It is a row where whatever happened is smaller than this run can see, which rules out a large effect and says nothing about a small one.

derived.name: THE BILL
derived.what: Every card in the branch, sorted by where it physically is: already in the deck, in a box, in another deck, or not owned.
derived.why: The only cost figure in the report. `buy` is money; `elsewhere` is a card that has to come out of a deck that is currently sleeved.

forge.biggest_hit.what: the largest single-source combat damage dealt to a player, per game
forge.biggest_hit.why: one big lifelinker connecting reads differently from twelve tokens; this is the number that separates them

forge.combat_damage_dealt_to_players.what: combat damage our seat dealt to players, mean per game, with the median beside it because the sample is mostly zeros with a tail
forge.combat_damage_dealt_to_players.why: the shape of the kill on a combat deck; the figure that fell 29.07 -> 18.20 when a go-wide refactor cut every lord

forge.commander_resolved_rate.what: games in which the commander resolved at least once, over games played
forge.commander_resolved_rate.why: a FLOOR on commander access under Forge's AI — the deck's plan cannot start until it does

forge.drain_dealt.what: life LOSS dealt to opponents that was not damage, per game — Blood Artist, Vito, Sanguine Bond — credited to the seat whose life-loss ability resolved last that turn; a floor
forge.drain_dealt.why: the drain engine's output, which no damage total sees

forge.eliminated_turn.what: the global turn our seat was eliminated, mean over the games it lost
forge.eliminated_turn.why: survival; conditional on losing, so a deck that wins more can read worse here for dying faster in the games it still loses

forge.empty_hand_turns.what: own turns that ended with ZERO cards in hand, per game — exact under the telemetry patch, absent on a plain record
forge.empty_hand_turns.why: the complaint itself, counted: a turn spent with nothing to rebuild with

forge.evasive_damage_share.what: share of our combat damage to players dealt by sources with flying, trample, menace or another evasion keyword, per game with any combat damage (from the deck's own keywords, so our seat only)
forge.evasive_damage_share.why: 'big scary vampires with all sorts of ways to hurt people' — measured as the damage that got through because it could not be blocked

forge.extra_draw_per_turn.what: cards that reached our hand from the library BEYOND the natural draw step, per own turn, per game — (library_to_hand minus one per own turn, minus nothing for the first turn on the play) over own turns; a wheel, a cantrip, a tutor and a death-trigger draw all count, a mulligan does not
forge.extra_draw_per_turn.why: the draw the DECK added, so a list that refills its hand reads apart from one that only draws for the turn; telemetry records only

forge.first_attack_turn.what: the GLOBAL turn of our seat's first declared attack, mean over the games in which it attacked at all
forge.first_attack_turn.why: how long the AI sat on the deck; conditional, so a branch that attacks in more games can read WORSE here by attacking late in games it used to skip

forge.kills_by_ability.what: opposing permanents that left the battlefield directly after one of our activated abilities resolved, per game — Vish Kal's -X/-X, an outlet's kill; a ceiling per card
forge.kills_by_ability.why: removal the deck does with its own creatures rather than with spells

forge.life_gained.what: life gained per game, all sources (the record splits it: lifelink, trigger, other)
forge.life_gained.why: the gain half of a gain/drain deck, and Vito's and Sanguine Bond's input

forge.life_removed_total.what: every point of life this seat removed from opponents in a game — combat damage plus noncombat damage plus drain, summed, with the median beside the mean because the sample has a long tail
forge.life_removed_total.why: the only axis that cannot be gamed by trading one kind of output for a smaller amount of another: drain-v1 and boss-v1 each raised drain by ~4.5 while losing ~17 combat damage, and this row would have said so

forge.noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players.what: damage to players that did not come from combat, per game — an ETB pinger, a Purphoros, a direct-damage spell
forge.noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players.why: the output an ENTRY payoff produces, which needs no attack step and no blocker maths; the champion makes 8.04 eminence tokens a game and converts almost none of them

forge.win_rate.what: wins over DECIDED games at the named pod (clock-outs have no winner and leave the denominator), pooled across every run of that list under one harness
forge.win_rate.why: the only figure with external validity on this bench, read against the table's null rather than a quarter

board power @T6.what: Total power on the battlefield at the end of turn 6.
board power @T6.why: The deck's turn-6 threat, before any of it has connected. It is what a table sees and decides to answer, and it moves earlier than damage does.

damage @T10.scale: one turn's damage, so 40.0 would be lethal in a single swing from an opponent at full life — not a total across the game
damage @T10.what: Damage dealt to the single goldfish opponent ON turn 10, averaged over every game — the clock at its tenth turn, not a running total. The cumulative series does not exist for this pillar; `mean_cumulative_event_damage_by_turn` is the only running total the model keeps, and it covers event damage alone.
damage @T10.why: The headline output figure and the one a doubler moves. It has no ceiling, so unlike the kill rate it keeps separating two lists after both of them already win.

extra cards by T8.scale: against the 8 cards every deck draws for free by then
extra cards by T8.what: Cards drawn BEYOND the one-a-turn draw step, cumulative to the end of turn 8, averaged over every game. Counts only draw the model can price — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and a trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter. Activated, X-based, sacrifice-gated and death-triggered draw are NOT counted and the cards are named in the goldfish artifact.
extra cards by T8.why: "Vampires on board, nothing in hand, no way to rebuild" is the most-repeated line in this deck's log, and until 2026-08-28 the model could not see it: it drew one card a turn whatever the list said. Read it against the count of draw cards, not alone — a deck listing twelve draw sources whose modelled figure is one has almost no UNCONDITIONAL card advantage, and that is a fact about the deck rather than a limit of the parser.

hand can act by T3.scale: against the keep rate itself — this is a property of the seven cards kept, assuming no draws
hand can act by T3.what: The share of kept opening hands containing a nonland card the hand's own lands can pay for by turn three, counting at most three land drops and no draws.
hand can act by T3.why: A stricter threshold than the 2-5 lands rule the model actually mulligans by, and it is REPORTED rather than enforced, so it cannot restate a figure on any deck. It separates "this hand had lands" from "this hand could do something" — the distinction behind a two-land keep that never got going.

hoard @T10.what: Treasures sitting in the hoard at the end of turn 10, averaged over every game.

Death-triggered drain and damage are NOT modelled on this deck: it declares no `model_deaths` rate, so nothing dies in this simulation and Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Pashalik Mons and Bastion of Remembrance contribute nothing to any damage or kill row. objective.why: v1.2.0 at BRACKET 4 — the pilot's call, 2026-10-01, after drain-v1's 200-game arm read as an overall downgrade: 'bring back bloodthirsty conqueror... let's go full on Tier 4... I want something that can close or win by T6'. READING B IS REVERSED: Conqueror stays, so Conqueror+Vito and Conqueror+Sanguine Bond are two-card infinites the deck carries by construction and that is accepted. THE LOOP IS NOT THE PLAN: nothing tutors for it, Exquisite Blood stays out. The clock target is stated honestly as T7-T8 — a T6 POD kill needs ~120 life across three opponents and Sanctum Seeker with six attackers doubled by Bloodletter is ~12 to each a combat. WHAT drain-v1 TAUGHT (same harness, 200 games each arm): drain 6.59 -> 10.66, +4.07 [0.45, 7.69] EXCLUDES ZERO, so the five adds that played do raise drain; but life_gained -14.5, biggest_hit -1.95 and combat damage -16.6 mean (median -3.0, tail-driven) all excluded zero, and essentially all of that was Conqueror's departure — he was the gain engine and the deck's biggest body. So: Conqueror in, the five proven adds in, the lords NOT cut as deeply (7 -> 5 plus Shared Animosity, where drain-v1 went 7 -> 4), and bracket-4 mana. THE OBJECTIVE IS DELIBERATELY THE SAME LINE drain-v1 MISSED (10.66 against >= 12), so the two branches are directly comparable and the question is exactly 'does Conqueror's return plus Mirkwood Bats and Indulging Patrician clear it'. Combat damage, biggest hit, life gained and win rate are read as exploratory with their intervals, and the branch is NOT proposable if combat damage or biggest hit falls with an interval excluding zero. Harness PINNED as before: standard-v3 / overrides 8c347642 / mm-edgar-vampires (aif7c3b6a8) / patches c22ecaf3. No pay-X sweeper is staged, so the PumpAllAi patch is deliberately NOT made yet and the champion's 200 games stay the comparison. EVERY ADD IS CAST-CHECKED BEFORE THE ARM (the 2026-10-01 gate).
